law_refs.notes: A roadway obstruction might close the right half and affect where the driver may travel; two-way width and the obstruction’s location must be checked.

A winding road can contain a curve. This rule becomes live only if the driver goes left of center and the view is obstructed enough to create a hazard; the named obstruction need not be a sight obstruction.
Direct U-turn safety rule; the obstruction and winding geometry can matter to whether the turn can be made safely. Its cited exceptions require separate facts.
Directly concerns reversal on a curve. Check whether this winding-road segment is a curve and whether approaching drivers can see the vehicle within 500 feet.
A U-turn changes direct course. The signal duties depend on whether a pedestrian or another vehicle may be affected. NRS-484B-768-1 addresses the analogous cyclist/scooter turning event.
The U-turn changes course; signal distance depends on business/residential district versus other area.
Reasonable-speed duty applies while driving; a winding road and obstruction are relevant conditions. The extracted subject is driver; cyclist/scooter speed duties are separately listed.
Broad prohibition on an endangering speed; no speed or endangerment outcome is assumed.
Absolute speed cap applies on a highway; exceeding it is unlikely during a U-turn, but speed before the maneuver is unspecified.
The law expressly names a winding highway and possible special hazards; it is a direct layout match, with speed reduction assessed only if necessary.
Broad reckless-driving prohibition; the scenario does not itself establish willful or wanton disregard.

context_refs.notes: A winding road could also be divided, but no divided roadway or median is given. Review only if the turn crosses a divider.
Would apply if an official device governs this location, such as a no-U-turn sign; none is stated. This is the general device-obedience rule behind NRS-484B-403-2.
Requires an active school zone or school-crossing zone, which the scenario does not specify. The U-turn is the direct match.
Requires a governing no-U-turn device, not given. LVMC-11-40-080 describes the same signed U-turn restriction for a cyclist/scooter subject.
Requires a business district; a winding road could be in one, but district and intersection/divided-highway exceptions are unknown.
Could arise if the driver stops or sharply slows for the obstruction or turn and another vehicle is immediately behind; neither fact is given.
Would apply if a speed limit is posted for this segment; no sign or speed is specified.
Could matter if slowing for the obstruction impedes following traffic and reduced speed is not necessary for safety; no following traffic is stated.
Could matter if the driver comes to a full stop on the roadway and blocks traffic while negotiating the obstruction; a safety-necessary stop is excepted.
A U-turn at a fire-station entrance would be covered, but neither a fire station nor Las Vegas location is stated.
Only if this road is within the City and no different speed limit is posted.
General attention duty for vehicle operation; city-law applicability depends on the scenario location.
General careful-operation duty on a City highway; the winding road and obstruction could affect prudent operation, but City location is unknown.

law_refs.notes: Direct rule for a bicycle, e-bike or scooter turning from a direct course; the obstruction affects the safety judgment. Signal exceptions depend on lane and safe-handling facts. Analogous driver turning event: NRS-484B-413-1.
If a hand/arm turn signal is required under NRS-484B-768-1, this law specifies how the rider gives it; the act of signaling is not stated.

The law expressly treats fixed or moving objects and surface hazards as reasons riding near the right may be unsafe. Check whether the obstruction impedes access to the right; this is the rider-side analogue of a road-position issue.

context_refs.notes: Could matter if the cyclist/scooter rider intentionally interferes with a motor vehicle while making the U-turn; no motor vehicle or intent is stated.
Applies to the electric-scooter subtype on a roadway; not to every cyclist in this actor variant. A local ordinance can alter the rule.
Would apply if an official signal, sign or device governs this rider; none is stated. LVMC-11-40-080 specifically addresses a no-U-turn sign.
Requires an authorized no-U-turn sign and operation in the City; neither is stated. It addresses the same signed turn restriction for riders that NRS-484B-403-2 addresses for drivers.
General reasonable-speed duty for the bicycle subtype only, if in the City; winding geometry and obstruction affect conditions.
General unsafe-speed/reckless-behavior restriction for electric-bicycle or scooter subtype in the City; not a claim that any stunt occurs.
